seb-certified-summary: Oklahoma State Election Board, meeting packet of November 15, 2022: 'MESA - Election Summary Results'

notes: The Board's own results file for the general election of 11/8/2022, from the Export menu of its results page, which was marked 'Official Results' when the file was saved through a browser on 2026-10-03 (this is that copy: its SHA-256 is the one recorded then). The results site refuses scripts, so nothing is asked of it here. The county election boards certify their counties' results; the State Election Board certifies the federal, state, legislative and judicial contests and the state questions. Listed on https://oklahoma.gov/elections/elections-results/election-results/2022-election-results/2022-november-general-election.html.

The summary laid before the State Election Board at the meeting where it certified the general election (printed 11/14/2022). Listed on https://oklahoma.gov/elections/about-us/meeting-notices-agendas-and-minutes-archives/2022-agendas-and-minutes.html. Its figures are the totals of the contests it prints. Its pages are printed sideways; the text is rebuilt line by line from where each piece of type stands.
gaps: Oklahoma prints a race on the November ballot only when it is contested (the Clerk of the House's statistics: 'According to Oklahoma law, the names of those with no opposition are not printed on the ballot'), so a candidate unopposed at filing, or elected outright in the June primary or the August runoff, has no November result here.
City, town and school board elections held at other times

Most Oklahoma city, town and school board elections are held in the spring, not in November; only the city, town, school and fire district contests and questions that were on this November ballot are here.
